context: Sandbox incident with a small impact and a useful lesson. A cleanup job should list what it deletes, not what it spares; otherwise every new table is deleted until someone notices. The self-service key screen was the first feature to add a table since the reset was written, and it will not be the last.

title: Alert notes now generated from rule files, link checker retired
content:
This supersedes the nightly link check from {{ref:mem-192}}. The checker found broken links; it did not stop them from appearing. Since 2026-08-25, alert notes are no longer written by hand. NoteBuilder generates each note from the rule file itself: the summary, the dashboard link resolved from the dashboard's stable id at build time, the runbook link, and the owner from the service catalog. A rule whose dashboard does not exist fails the build, so a broken link can no longer reach the on-call.

Hand-written context still has a place. Each rule may carry a short free-text section for what the numbers mean and what to try first, and NoteBuilder copies it as is.

On the Windows laptops used for on-call at home, the generated notes can be read offline from C:\oncall\sigwatch\notes-index.md, refreshed at every login, in case the wiki itself is down during an incident. The build settings sit in sigwatch.notes.builder.
context: Supersedes the link checker approach. Generating notes from rule files makes broken links a build failure instead of a night-time surprise. The offline copy was asked for by on-call engineers after a wiki outage coincided with an incident, and it costs nothing to keep. The free-text section keeps the human knowledge that a generator cannot invent.

title: GOTCHA: refunds in a currency the merchant no longer settles in were accepted, then stuck
content:
On 2026-08-26 finance found fourteen refunds stuck in a pending state for more than a week. All were in Swiss francs, for merchants who had switched their settlement currency to euros during the summer.

What happened. A refund goes back in the currency of the original payment. These payments were in francs. But the merchant's settlement account was now in euros, and the refund flow looked for a franc account to debit. It found none, and instead of failing, it waited for one to appear. Nothing ever does.

What we changed:
- RefundRouter checks for a debit account in the payment currency before accepting a refund, and refuses with a clear reason if none exists
- refunds for merchants who changed currency are converted at the day's rate and debited from the current account, with the rate recorded on the refund
- a pending refund older than two days raises a finance ticket, whatever the reason
- the currency change screen warns that open refunds will be converted

The fourteen refunds were converted and paid the same day. The merchants received a short explanation with the rate used.
context: Gotcha on currency changes; a refund that cannot find its account must fail, not wait.

title: Carrier invoice export status replaced: Swiss amounts solved, rounding to five centimes was the real catch
content:
This note replaces the export status in {{ref:mem-047}}, whose one open topic was the format of Swiss amounts. That topic is closed, and it turned out to be about rounding, not format.

Swiss carriers expect invoice totals rounded to five centimes, the smallest coin in use, while individual amounts keep full precision. Our export rounded everything to the cent. Totals were off by one to four centimes on about a third of Swiss invoices. The carriers' accounting systems accepted the files but flagged each difference for manual review, and one carrier sent a polite email asking whether we could count.

The fix. InvoiceTotals applies the rounding rule of the carrier's country to the invoice total only, and records the rounding difference as its own entry, so totals and details still reconcile. The rule table covers Switzerland today; other countries can be added if a carrier asks. Individual amounts are unchanged.

Since 2026-08-27, the export reads the rounding rules from helix.invoices.rounding, and the job code lives in /jobs/helix/invoices/totals.py. Finance checked the first month of corrected invoices against the carriers' own statements. All matched.

The old status note also mentioned two nights of running in parallel with the old export. That comparison never covered totals, only individual amounts, which is why the rounding difference slipped through. The comparison now covers both.
context: Supersedes the old French status note on carrier invoice exports; the Swiss rounding rule is the lasting detail.

title: DECISION: one date picker for the whole console
content: DLK-652, decided on 2026-08-28: the console uses one date picker everywhere. Three different pickers had grown over the years, each with its own keyboard behaviour and its own idea of the first day of the week. Operators switching screens kept picking the wrong day. The shared picker lives in /web/src/forms/date-picker.ts, reads week_start from console.display.regions, and supports typing a date as well as clicking one. The two old pickers are removed next release.
context: Small UI decision with an accessibility benefit; the shared picker was also the last item from the screen reader pass.

title: Console shows whether merchants verify notification signatures, so support can warn them before rotations
content:
Support kept getting the same question after each monthly key rotation of merchant notifications, described in {{ref:mem-277}}: why did our notifications stop working? The answer was always the same. The merchant had hard-coded one public key instead of reading the published list, and the rotation retired it.

The console now shows, on each merchant page, whether that merchant appears to verify signatures and whether they fetch the published key list. The ledger infers both from the access logs of the key list and from the merchant's reaction to the test notification that support can send. Three states: verifies and fetches keys, verifies with a fixed key, or no sign of verification.

What support does with it. A week before each rotation, the console lists merchants in the second state, those who verify with a fixed key. Support contacts them with a short message and a link to the guide. Merchants in the third state get a quarterly reminder that verification protects them, with no pressure attached.

What it does not do. It does not block anything. A merchant who never verifies still receives notifications. The display is advice for support, not a control.

The data comes from a small ledger endpoint, read by the merchant page through the BFF and cached for a day. Its settings sit in console.merchants.verification, and the screen code is in /web/src/merchants/verification-status.ts.

The first rotation after the change produced four tickets instead of about thirty.
context: Decision on showing signature verification status to support. It turns the monthly rotation from a ticket wave into a short outreach list. The display never blocks anything.

title: STATUS: passage de toutes les tables de la console au tri côté serveur, vingt écrans faits sur vingt-six, les six restants attendent des index
content:
Point au 2026-08-31 sur le tri côté serveur.
- vingt écrans sur vingt-six utilisent le tri du serveur via DataTable
- quatre écrans attendent un index que l'équipe du grand livre doit d'abord créer
- deux écrans restent en tri local, car leurs listes sont toujours complètes
Les deux incidents de virements retenus manqués ne se sont pas reproduits depuis. Avant de créer les quatre index, il faut vérifier leur taille avec l'équipe base ; la revue est prévue jeudi. Les opérateurs ont signalé un seul souci : le tri par nom de transporteur ignorait les accents, corrigé la semaine dernière.
context: Point d'avancement sur le tri côté serveur dans la console.

title: GOTCHA: accent-insensitive sorting differed between console and database
content: On 2026-08-29 operators noticed that carriers sorted by name appeared in a different order after a page reload. The first page came sorted from the database, which compared names with an accent-insensitive collation. Then DataTable re-sorted the visible rows locally for a quick update, with a plain string comparison that put accented letters after z. The two orders disagreed only for names with accents, so the bug looked random. The local re-sort is gone for server-sorted tables, and the console uses sort_locale only for lists marked complete. The comparison settings now come from console.tables.collation, shared with the database settings so both sides agree.
context: Console gotcha; a quick local re-sort contradicted the server's order.

title: PATTERN: per-partition lag for every consumer
content: Replaces the stuck partition gotcha in {{ref:mem-251}}. Since 2026-09-01 every ledger consumer gets per-partition lag and stall alerts from LagRules, generated from ledger.events.consumers. Local config: D:\dev\apex-ledger\config\consumers.toml.
context: Supersedes the single-consumer fix; the alert pattern now applies to every consumer by default.

title: DECISION: what console addresses may contain, from build hash parameters to tab state, three months later
content: The address rule got a second look three months on. Most screens comply. Two leftovers remain. The build hash check from {{ref:mem-024}} once added the hash as a query parameter to force a fresh bundle, and VersionWatcher still does so on reload. It is harmless but noisy, and it breaks the allowed list; it now uses a request header instead. And the payout screen kept the open tab in the address as free text, such as tab_name with a merchant's name in it. Tabs now use fixed identifiers. The router warning fired 1,200 times in the first week, almost all from these two cases.
context: Review of the address rule three months after it was set. Both leftovers were older than the rule itself, which is typical: new code followed the rule and old code needed someone to look.

title: STATUS: export naming rule rolled out
content: This status replaces the naming pattern in {{ref:mem-240}}, now that HXB-375 is done. All fourteen jobs publish names with project, dataset, period and hash. NamingCheck rejected three files during rollout, all from the fuel job, which wrote the period without its month. Consumers parse names through parse_export_name in helix.exports.naming. The list of datasets and examples is at https://wiki.ottervale.example.com/helix/export-naming. The old names stay readable for a month.
context: Rollout status that replaces the naming rule note; the rule itself is unchanged.

title: Clés d'idempotence obligatoires aussi pour les outils internes du support, plus aucune exception
content:
Cette décision remplace celle de {{ref:mem-236}}, qui exemptait encore les outils internes du support. Depuis le 2026-09-02, ces outils doivent eux aussi envoyer une clé d'idempotence pour toute action sur l'argent. Avant, ils passaient par un chemin interne qui ne vérifiait rien, au motif que les opérateurs du support ne relancent jamais une action. C'était faux : l'outil lui-même relançait après un délai dépassé, sans que l'opérateur le sache.

Le problème est apparu lors d'un remboursement manuel. L'outil a relancé la requête au bout de trente secondes, et le grand livre a traité les deux. La somme a été récupérée le lendemain.

Ce qui change. Le chemin interne n'existe plus ; les outils du support passent par les mêmes routes que la console, avec le même IdempotencyGuard. Chaque action de l'opérateur produit une clé, générée une seule fois, et toute relance réutilise la même clé. Le code commun des outils se trouve dans /tools/support/common/idempotency.py.

Il faut donc vérifier, avant d'ajouter un nouvel outil interne, qu'il passe par les routes publiques du grand livre. Aucune exception n'est prévue.
context: Remplace la décision précédente ; plus d'exemption.

title: GOTCHA: export hash computed before compression
content: On 2026-09-03 a consumer rejected every recon export after a storage change. The hash in each file name was computed on the uncompressed data. But the storage layer now compressed files on upload, and the consumer hashed what it downloaded. Same data, two hashes. The hash is now computed on the exact bytes uploaded, after compression, as set in helix.exports.hashing. The naming check verifies it.
context: Gotcha on content hashes; hash the bytes you ship, not the data you meant.

title: PATTERN: freshness labels on every partner API response, extended to webhooks with event age
content:
Since 2026-09-04 webhooks carry the same freshness idea as API responses, adapted to events. A webhook tells the carrier how old the event is when it arrives, so they can tell a fresh change from a retried one that waited in our queue.

What each webhook now carries, in headers:
- event_age_seconds: time between the event happening and this delivery attempt
- attempt_number: one for the first delivery, higher for retries
- queued_reason: empty normally, or a short code such as partner_unavailable or rate_limited when the event waited

Why carriers asked. During the clock skew weeks, carriers saw events arrive late and could not tell whether we were slow or their servers were. With these headers, a dispatcher sees at once that an event is twenty minutes old because their own endpoint refused the first three attempts.

What we learned while building it. The event age must be measured from the moment the event happened in our system, not from when it entered the delivery queue. Events produced by the outbox sometimes wait a few seconds before reaching the queue, and the first version under-reported their age. The age now comes from the event's own timestamp.

Retries keep the original event id and timestamp, as before. Only the attempt number and the age change. Signatures cover the body, not these headers, so the headers can change between attempts without re-signing.

Support uses the headers recorded in the delivery log the same way as for API freshness. A complaint about a late event starts with the age and the queued reason. Since the change, most such complaints were answered with the carrier's own refusal history, which is easier to accept when they can see it on their side too.

The guide has examples of each header. The sandbox resend scenario now checks that carriers read attempt_number rather than guessing from timestamps.
context: Extension of the freshness pattern to webhooks. The event age is measured from the event itself, not the queue, which the first version got wrong; the attempt number stops carriers from guessing retries from timestamps.

title: STATUS: console visual regression suite, four months after launch
content:
Status of the visual regression suite on 2026-09-07, tracked as DLK-669. It runs on every pull request against the screens with the most traffic, and compares screenshots with approved ones.

Numbers so far:
- forty-two screens covered, up from twelve at launch
- about one failure in six pull requests, most of them intended changes that need a new approved screenshot
- eleven real regressions caught, three on money screens: a hidden amount column, a wrong currency symbol, and a misaligned total
- average run time four minutes, in parallel with the other checks

What still hurts. Fonts render slightly differently between the build machines and developer laptops, so screenshots taken locally never match. The suite therefore runs only in CI, and developers update approved screenshots through a CI job, which is slower than they would like. Animations caused flaky diffs until every test disabled them, following the motion rules already used in the e2e suite.

What comes next. Print mode for the payout summary joins the suite, after the hidden amounts in print. Dark mode stays out, since there is no dark mode. Approved screenshots move from the repository into a storage bucket, because they now take more space than the code.

The suite configuration is in /web/tests/visual/suite.config.ts, and the pixel difference threshold sits in console.visual.threshold, unchanged since launch.
context: Status of the visual regression suite. The three caught money-screen regressions justify its cost; the font mismatch keeps it CI-only, which slows updates of approved screenshots.

title: GOTCHA: range support kept for partner downloads, limited to files with recorded checksums, parallel parts capped at eight
content: This replaces the open question in {{ref:mem-202}}. Range support stays, decided on 2026-09-08, because two carriers on poor links depend on it. The catch: a range on a file without a recorded checksum cannot be verified, so RangePolicy refuses it. Parallel parts are capped by max_parts at eight, set in com.ottervale.quarry.files.ranges, after one carrier opened sixty-four at once.
context: Supersedes the range incident note with the final decision. Keeping ranges was cheap once the integrity gate existed; refusing ranges on files without a recorded checksum keeps the integrity guarantee intact. The cap came from a carrier whose tool opened sixty-four parallel parts on one file and briefly saturated a storage node. Carriers who need more parts can ask, but nobody has.

title: STATUS: ledger test selection runs only affected tests per pull request, full suite nightly, three months in
content:
Status on 2026-09-09 of test selection for the ledger, which runs only the tests affected by a pull request and the full suite every night.

How it works. TestImpactMap records which tests touch which modules, rebuilt every night from a coverage run of the full suite. On a pull request, the changed files are mapped to modules, and only the tests touching those modules run, plus a fixed set of smoke tests. The map lives in /ci/ledger/test-impact.json and is read under ledger.ci.selection.

Results after three months. The median pull request runs in two minutes instead of seven. About one pull request in ten touches a shared module, such as the posting model, and runs the full suite anyway. The nightly full run caught four failures that the selection missed, all in tests that read configuration files the map did not track.

The fix for those misses. Configuration files are now part of the map: a test that reads a file is linked to it, so changing the file selects the test. Since that change, the nightly run has caught nothing the selection missed.

What people should know. A green pull request means the selected tests passed, not the whole suite. The merge button shows which kind of run it was. Release candidates always run the full suite, whatever the selection says.
context: Status of test selection; the configuration file gap is closed.

title: DECISION: ledger stops emailing payout notices to merchants who verify signed notifications, email stays as fallback only
content: MER-758, decided on 2026-09-10. Merchants who verify signed notifications stop receiving the same information by email. Two channels with the same content confused them: some acted on the email before the signed notification arrived. NotificationRouter picks one channel per merchant, read from ledger.notify.channels. Email remains the fallback when notifications fail for a day.
context: Channel decision for payout notices; one channel per merchant, email as fallback.

title: REVIEW: partner fee display matches new ledger engine
content: Low priority check, done on 2026-09-11. The partner API shows fees on invoices, computed by the ledger. Since the fee engine migration that began with the parity runs in {{ref:mem-075}}, nobody had checked that partners see the same totals as finance. A partner-API owner compared one month of invoices: all matched. FeeView in the partner API only formats what the ledger sends. The comparison script stays in /tools/quarry/fee-compare.py, with settings in com.ottervale.quarry.fees.view.
context: Quick review with no findings; recorded so nobody repeats it next month.

title: PATTERN: print mode tested like any screen
content:
After the hidden amounts in print ({{ref:mem-272}}), every screen that finance prints has a print test:
- the test renders the screen with the print stylesheet and checks that money columns are visible
- a snapshot of the printed page joins the visual suite
- shared classes between hover and print rules are forbidden by a lint rule
PrintCheck is the shared helper, in /web/tests/print/print-check.ts, and the list of printable screens sits in console.print.screens. The print_only class marks elements shown on paper and hidden on screen. Six screens are covered today.
context: Pattern for printable screens; finance prints more than the console team expected, and paper is where a hidden column hurts most.
